overall: The Committee violated the OML by giving insufficient detail for one June 7 executive session topic and by failing to periodically review outstanding executive session minutes; no intentional violation found, and no further relief ordered.

allegations.summary: June 7 meeting notice listed executive session topics without enough detail; complainant said several topics lacked specifics.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee concedes that the notice should have identified the name(s) of the non-union personnel to be discussed under item 5, as this information would not have compromised the purpose for the executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the notice had to state which of the ten statutory executive session purposes was invoked for each item.
allegations.key_passage: A public body need not specifically identify the statutory purpose for the executive session, as long as the description of the topic makes clear which of the ten executive session purposes the public body is invoking.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged executive session notices dating back to 2016 lacked sufficient detail, a practice-wide claim without a specific date.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we decline to review these allegations because our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to identify the individuals who would participate in an executive session.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Committee did not periodically review its outstanding executive session minutes for possible release to the public.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee acknowledges that it did not review its outstanding executive session minutes for potential release at reasonable interviews.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the violations were intentional; the AG considered whether intent was shown under G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c).
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the violations were not intentional.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
